recipes.name: Haddock Bubbly Bake
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly butter a 2 quart casserole dish.

Arrange fish fillets in the bottom of the prepared casserole dish, and sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste. Layer onion slices over fish. Spread cream of mushroom soup over all, and top with shredded cheese.
Bake in preheated oven for about 40 minutes, or until bubbly and fish flakes easily with a fork.

raw_recipe.headline: Haddock Bubbly Bake
raw_recipe.description: This is really great served with mashed potatoes and peas or veggie of your choice. This dish is a favorite of Nova Scotia, Canada.

review.reviewBody: This recipie is great! Try adding broccoli, it gives this recipie what it needs. It's the way we make it in Nova Scotia!

I melted a stick of butter in my casserole dish first then added 3 blocks of Icelandic haddock. Added salt and pepper and minced onions to the fish. Then I topped the fish with frozen diced potatoes and added a little more salt and pepper with some Mrs. Dash salt free seasoning. I mixed two cans of cream of mushroom soup with one can of carnations evaporated milk. Poured half of the mix over the potatoes and fish then added broccoli on top of the potatoes and poured the remaining soup mixture over that. Topped it off with mild cheddar cheese and a little bit of Mrs.Dash. Cooked it in oven for 50 minutes at 350•. DELICIOUS! Next time I’ll try golden mushroom soup.

When I make this dish...I sauté onions and garlic in olive oil, once they are translucent I add garlic powder, parsley, green onion, salt & pepper and a dash of paprika and a can of cocktail shrimp liquid drained. Mix well and heat then a can of cream of mushroom soup and a can of cream of celery and using the empty can I add 1 and half cans of milk. Blend and warm all ingredients together... (this alone tastes wonderful ) I place my fish in a casserole dish pour my soup mixture on the cover with grated cheddar cheese (old) bake at 375....serve with mixed veggies and mashed potatoes. .....I'm a Scotia girl too!

The ingredients are a good basis for a quick and easy dinner. Three stars because I think a little difference in prep will make for better flavor. I sauteed sliced onions and mushrooms in a little butter. I splashed a little vermouth in, let it reduce and then stirred in 1/2 the mushroom soup. I spread this over a well-patted dry piece of haddock. I baked about 20 minutes. I added 1/4 c. of vermouth to the rest of the mushroom soup. I poured over the dish then baked 5 minutes more. After baking removed the haddock to a serving dish, sprinkled with the cheese and let it sit 10 minutes. Stirred the mushroom soup and veggies, then served the sauce separately. Turned out pretty good. A friend suggested a few chopped tomatoes on the top might even be nice. Served it with steamed broccoli and wild rice. Garlic mashed potatoes would be yummy too!

This was very delicious. I took advice from other reviewers and added broccoli. I also substituted green onions instead of regular onions. I steamed the broccoli for 10 mins before adding it to the fish. Then spooned the soup over fish and broccoli,added cheddar cheese and for a nice twist topped it off with crushed Ritz crackers. Baked 350 for 30 mins. My fiancee doesn't care for fish but he really liked this and had seconds.

Mmm. Comfort food. I used a garlic cream o' mush soup but I didn't think I would have enough sauce to drizzle on both the fish and the mashed potatoes I'd made (I also made sauteed apples from this site). I had about 8 oz. of light sour cream in the 'fridge, so put 1 tablespoon corn starch, 1/4 cup milk,1/2 teaspoon white pepper, and a dollop of Better than Bouillon lobster base in a jar and shook it. I mixed in the sour cream and added it to the soup on top the fish. So amazingly good, especially with the mashed potatoes and sauteed apples. Definately comfort food. :)

This was good. I used Kingfish instead of Haddock because that was what we caught and it was perfect as kingfish (aka - bluefish) is a fishy fish and the soup gave it a very pleasant flavor! I carmelized the onions and added several carmelized cloves of garlic as well. I also thined the soup a bit with skim milk so it wasn't so overbearing. We served it up a fresh salad, crusty bread and asparagus. I plan on making this again and using a condensenced shrimp bisque adding chopped shrimp to it and doubling the onion and garlic.

This was simply fantastic! So easy and SO SO SO delicious! I served it with peas and roasted potatoes...but mashed potatoes would be wonderful, too.
I used 2 cans of mushroom soup (instead of one), and I got this wonderful sauce (that tasted fantastic over the potatoes and peas!!) I only used 3/4 of an onion because it seemed like enough at the time - but now wish I had used more, as they were a nice addition (even my husband, who isn't a big fan of lots of onion, even remarked on how he enjoyed the onions). Also - I made this in a large baking dish, so I had a single layer of fish on the bottom. Not sure if that matters. This gets HIGH marks with us!

I'm from Nova Scotia too and have been making this recipe since I learned it in a Jr. High Home Economics class! My recipe is the same but uses slightly less fish and a lot less onion, plus a tablespoon of lemon juice. It can be baked at 450 for only 15 minutes or so. (In case you're in more of a rush!) It is also good with scallops or any other whitefish (cod, etc.) I usually serve it with rice and a steamed veggie such as broccoli, carrots or green beans. Going to try to make it in the slow cooker today!
This is a winner! Easy,and delicious. Like a few others,I sauted' the onions first,just til golden; I also topped the cheese with buttered,crushed Ritz cracker crumbs.Yum!

Just had this tonight, and it was a smash hit! I did make a few little tweaks, tho, thus the 4-star rating. I had never cooked with haddock before so, not knowing what to do with the skin, I left it on---it was fine. I seasoned the fish lightly with salt / pepper and some garlic powder; the mushroom soup I mixed with 3-4 tblsp of skim milk and the juice of a whole lemon. It was delicious!!! We will definitely be having this again in the future---thank you!!
Easy recipe to fix when you want something good and quick.
Used 1/2 the soup, but otherwise unchanged. Oh my goodness was it good! Next time I might add broccoli or asparagus. Served mine with crispy hash browns. 10 thumbs up!

Like others I tweaked this oldie but goodie. Juice of 1/2 a lemon, lazy garlic (jarred minced garlic), fine green beans, lemon zest, and a couple of pinches of Italian herbs were what I added . I used green onions instead of sliced because I was all out of regular onions. I first made this as a teenager from a recipe in a magazine, so my adds are related to that history.
I swapped out onions for broccoli and added a bread crumb & Parmesan cheese topping which formed a nice crust and locked in all the juices. It was a big success.
This was very good. Needs a little tweak but I will try this recipe again. I used cod fish instead of haddock. Had mashed potato and mustard pickles with it.

We loved it. I did add a little water to the soup. I also added garlic and onion powder to the soup. And Mrs. Dash Lemon Pepper seasoning bo th to the soup and on the fish. I didn't salt or pepper the fish. We are trying to lower our salt intake. We had it over fried rotini with onions.
Added broccoli which helped. Needed to cut the onion even thinner but do not like to use a Mandoline, too dangerous.
Delicious & an easy meal
This is delicious and SO simple to make
